items.title: Henry "Booker T." Glass Interview, 1972-05-19
items.q: Did you know Chicken Binks? I know Chicken. Was he very good? He was good.

ctx.x: Sun Rock Street. I don't know if you didn't know Bob. He stayed right there, Sun Rock Cross from the graveyard. The Sun Rock graveyard. I don't remember anybody named Bob that played mandolin. No, he used to play mandolin and he played violin.

I can't place him. Yeah. Bob. Did you know Chicken Binks? I know Chicken. Was he very good? He was good. Yeah, he was good. Well what was your very first music job that you ever played? Playing at the Plunk Plant. I was playing at the Plunk Plant.

That was your first job? Then I went to play for the Judd City Burser. We used to play. You see Garnier used to be the leader of the band and he died and I took the band over. And we played for the brothers. I can play in all them jobs. So that made me be the leader. That's the way we'd take it. When a member would die in the band, the other fellow would take over and wanted to take over. And then the other one would join in with us. So most every man you see out there done been a leader of a band. Jim Crow, all…
